newsitem.title: UK: Biocompatibles up again on positive commnet.
newsitem.headline: Biocompatibles up again on positive commnet.

text.p: Shares in Biocompatibles Plc pushed higher into record territory on Friday on positive press comment after the company received approval to market its new contact lens in the United States.

A report in the Daily Telegraph said the "superficially ludicrous" rating of the loss-making company was "not as ridiculous as it looks" and that its coating product -- which makes products more acceptable to the body --had enormous applications.
The Telegraph said "anyone with the shares should resist the temptation to take profits just yet".
The stock was up 42-1/2p at 14.17-1/2 stg by 0913 GMT -- about double its value at the end of 1996 -- in volume of 243,009 shares.
Separately, the Financial Times quoted chief executive Alistair Taylor as saying the company was in talks with a "major contact lens distributor" and "hoped to be able to make an announcement soon."

The FT said the company's "stent" product, used to keep constricted blood vessels open, was selling well less than two months after launch in Europe, with over 1,000 sold at between $1,300 and $1,500 each.
